title: Reports of OpenAI dissolving its Preparedness team
public_note: A single outlet's report, citing internal sources, that OpenAI folded its catastrophic-risk evaluation team into other groups; no second independent outlet or on-the-record OpenAI statement found yet.
reason: Wire-exclusive check (verification.md §2): the Financial Times reported OpenAI dissolved its 'Preparedness' team (the unit evaluating whether OpenAI's models pose serious/catastrophic biological and cyber risks) at the end of July 2026, reassigning its work to existing teams, citing internal sources; Greg Brockman reportedly said the company has 'woven safety work more tightly into model development.' Every other outlet found (the-decoder.com, forum reposts) traces to the single FT report -- no independent second source. FT itself is inaccessible to direct fetch (blocked); the Brockman quote is only known via the-decoder's paraphrase of FT, not confirmed on openai.com, Brockman's own X account, or any OpenAI statement. openai.com's frontier-risk framework page also returned blocked on fetch this cycle, so could not be checked directly for any contradicting or confirming detail. This is a business/organizational claim requiring >=2 independent Tier<=2 sources or a company statement/filing, which is not met. dedup-check returned a moderate match (score 0.4) against openai-safety-heidecke-departure (also watching, unpublished) -- read that entry: it covers a distinct earlier event (Johannes Heidecke's mid-July departure and folding of Safety Systems into Research under Mia Glaese), not the Preparedness team specifically (previously led by Aleksander Madry, then Joaquin Quiñonero Candela). Related (both are 2026 OpenAI safety-org restructuring events in the same broader pattern -- Superalignment 2024, Mission Alignment Feb 2026, Safety Systems/Heidecke mid-July 2026, Preparedness end-of-July 2026/reported mid-Aug) but not the same claim; opened as a standalone watching entry rather than merged into the Heidecke entry, since neither is published and the underlying facts differ.
watch: A second, independently-sourced outlet (not relaying FT) confirming the Preparedness team's dissolution or reassignment details
An on-the-record OpenAI statement, blog post, or updated frontier-risk framework page addressing this specifically
Confirmation or denial of the exact Greg Brockman quote and its context

Recommended hold. Not published; opened as watching.

2026-08-18 c1 (night 2): Material development -- OpenAI issued an on-record denial today: a spokesperson stated "We have not disbanded the Preparedness team" (per The Next Web and Technology.org, both 8/18; Technology.org 403-blocked, quote via The Next Web). OpenAI confirms only that Dylan Scandinaro moved off leading Preparedness to work on recursive-self-improvement safety, and says research leaders across cybersecurity/bio-chem/self-improvement risk report to its head of safety. This satisfies the 'on-record OpenAI statement' watch item, but it CONTRADICTS the 'dissolved' framing rather than confirming it -- the claim as originally framed is now disputed, not confirmed, and should not be published as stated. All other coverage still traces to the single paywalled FT report; TechCrunch's independence unresolved. A reframed story ('OpenAI disputes report it dissolved Preparedness team') could be considered on its own merits in a future cycle. Still watching (original claim); gate still fails.

2026-08-18 c2 (night 2) recheck: New same-night Axios exclusive (Ina Fried, "OpenAI to rewrite its safety rules post-Hugging Face," axios.com/2026/08/18/openai-pause-astra-preparedness-framework, surfaced via Techmeme 18:10 UTC) plus OpenAI's own Tier-0 post ("Pacing model development in an era of cyber-critical capabilities," openai.com/index/pacing-model-development-cyber-capabilities/; both openai.com and axios.com 403-blocked to direct fetch as usual, content triangulated via search snippets and independent outlet coverage) confirm OpenAI paused RL training on its newest (Astra-generation) models for just over two weeks, hardened/red-teamed research environments and expanded monitoring after the Hugging Face breach and Astra's provisional Critical cyber-threshold finding (both already-published stories, not new events) -- and, the new detail, says it will evolve/rewrite the Preparedness FRAMEWORK (the 2023-vintage risk-threshold document), planning to involve outside organizations. NOT wire-exclusive: independently corroborated same-day by Time (Alex Heath, exclusive on-record Altman + Pachocki quotes, distinct from Axios's Altman quote), The Verge, Wired and The Decoder, each with its own headline/framing. Well-sourced (Tier-0 + 4 independent Tier-2 outlets), strong candidate for a future full verify+publish cycle -- likely as its own story or an in-place update to the already-published openai-astra-critical-cyber-capabilities entry (whose open_obligation/revisit_after 2026-08-21 this would satisfy early) -- but it concerns the Preparedness FRAMEWORK (policy document) and general safety-practice changes, not the Preparedness TEAM's staffing or existence, so it neither confirms nor denies THIS entry's 'dissolved the team' claim and does not move the wire-exclusive gate on the original claim. Logged here as cross-reference context for whichever cycle drafts that story. Still watching (original claim); gate still fails. Not actioned as a new story this cycle -- time budget went to two other candidates (Harvey Tenet, GLM-5.3); flagged in the cycle report for cycle 3.
